$comment: Index grouping for the skills.sh ecosystem.  Auto-indexers crawl skills/*/SKILL.md in a public repository.  Each entry below groups one skill on a single page.

skills.name: claim-ledger
skills.description: 13 pinned facts, 8 independent trap re-derivations. Binds every outcome an AI coding agent asserts to a check that can be run and can fail, and reports the ones that are unverified, refuted by their own check, or evidenced by a command that looked at nothing. Exit codes are the only assertion vocabulary: no LLM judge exceeded AUROC 0.65, so a judgement step would make the gate worse than the thing it gates. Does not judge whether the work is any good, and does not check prose.

skills.name: elohim
skills.description: Checksum-pinned numerical-instrument gate: 16 pinned facts, 6 independent trap re-derivations, a source hygiene lint, and a proven tamper test.

skills.name: elohim-harness
skills.description: The shared gate, not a fact-pinning skill. It holds no ledger and no instrument of its own and has 0 pinned facts and 0 traps to report. It runs the pin, fact, trap and hygiene gates against any skill directory named by --skill-dir, so the other six entries in this index each need no gate code of their own. Every count in every other entry was measured by this harness.

skills.name: estimator-bias
skills.description: 15 pinned facts, 7 independent trap re-derivations. Deflates a cubic to prove a Pisot decay rate exactly, fits the same rate from the data, and reports the gap over four ranges in units of the fit's own standard error.

skills.name: invariant-hunter
skills.description: 3 pinned facts, 5 independent trap re-derivations. An honest negative: it measures a claimed Collatz conserved quantity and a derived ghost seed and returns the measurement that shows neither is structure.

skills.name: pay-signal
skills.description: 9 pinned facts, 5 independent trap re-derivations, and a dated Hacker News corpus committed as a golden fixture. Separates stated preference, which costs its speaker nothing, from revealed preference, which costs money, migration effort or a private workaround, and reports which needs have no verified position rather than ranking them anyway. The measurement that motivated it: a quarter of a demand-shaped corpus is the author selling the answer. Its honest negative is that the classifier's revealed base is nearly empty, so the instrument withdraws its own rank-shift figure and leaves only the counts standing.

skills.name: precision-budget
skills.description: 9 pinned facts, 6 independent trap re-derivations. Derives the working-digit budget for a Pisot bound from the formula, then measures whether it is sufficient and shows the same quantity collapsing on a starved budget.

skills.name: reproducibility
skills.description: 6 pinned facts, 7 independent trap re-derivations. The tripwire, not a sixth measurement: it runs every sibling instrument and classifies the shard each one produced by the Python version that produced it, then fails when a shard lands outside the pinned table. The honest negative it carries is that the byte-identical-across-the-matrix claim was false for exactly one instrument, because CPython 3.12 made sum() a Neumaier compensated summation.

skills.name: tolerance-prover
skills.description: 23 pinned facts, 7 independent trap re-derivations. Measures the tightness of the Pisot bound 2 for the tribonacci and plastic constants and establishes that it is a supremum no finite n attains.
